Here will by simple help message
Here will be information about selected tile and units on it
Here will be information about selected tile and units on it
Lost city rumor: a scout entering here finds out what it holds.
Claimed land of %s: not paid, %s gold.
If you use it without paying, the settlement's alarm toward you rises by 5 once at the first use and by 2 each turn while the square stays in use.
The land cannot be paid for now: not enough gold, or the offer has changed.
The offer has changed. Nothing was paid; review it and choose again.
Nothing is paid now. The price is paid only when you confirm the colony name; canceling then pays nothing.
%s gold for native land will be paid when the colony is founded.
The colony will use claimed native land without paying.
The land payment was made and the square stays paid for.
Press N for native settlement details.
No native settlement is known yet.
Choose an action below. Closing this window changes nothing, and the unit stays where it is.
Your unit's role cannot do this.
Another colonist is already learning here.
A mission is already established here.
A rival mission holds this settlement; you may challenge it.
No other European power can be chosen as a target.
No defender of this settlement can be attacked from here.

Attack the %s settlement with the armed unit you chose. Every native brave on its square must be overcome, one battle at a time, before the settlement is taken. A lost battle ends the attack and the settlement stays.
Defenders on the square: %d. Settlement defense: +%d%%. First battle: your strength %d against %d, chance to win %d%%.
Spanish attack bonus: +%d%%. It applies to this native settlement attack only.
If the attack is carried out, the tribe's anger and this settlement's alarm toward your nation rise. A conquest raises them further.
You overcame %d defender(s) and conquered the settlement.
The attack ended after %d defender(s) were overcome. The settlement stands.
A treasure train worth %d gold now stands on the conquered square.
No treasure train was left in the settlement.
Your attacking unit lost its battle and was destroyed or left without its weapons.
A colonist or missionary of the settlement had no free square nearby and was lost with it.
The attack cannot be carried out now: the settlement, its defenders or your unit changed. Nothing was changed.
This European already demanded tribute here within the last ten turns.
Another unit holds this settlement's square, so no tribute can be demanded from here.
Demand tribute from the %s settlement with the unit you chose.
Your force: %s, from your unit and your own soldiers, dragoons and scouts on the squares around the settlement. Defenders on the square: %d, with strength %s.
The settlement's defense bonus is +%d%%. Your force must reach the defenders' strength to be paid.
Paid if your force reaches the defenders: the settlement gives up to %d gold from its treasury of %d.
Accepted, but the settlement's treasury is empty, so no gold is paid.
Refused if your force is below the defenders: no gold is paid.
Paid or refused, the tribe's anger (now %s) and this settlement's alarm (now %s) rise. No second demand to this settlement for ten turns.
The tribute cannot be demanded now: the settlement, its defenders, your units or the relations changed. Nothing was changed.
The settlement paid nothing: its treasury is empty.
The settlement refused the tribute. Nothing was paid, but its anger rose.
Your %s, who was learning in a conquered settlement of the %s tribe, found no free square nearby and died with it.
Your %s, who kept a mission in a conquered settlement of the %s tribe, found no free square nearby and died with it.
You conquered a settlement of the %s tribe; its defenders were overcome.
Incite the tribe against a European power
The native market cannot be opened now. Nothing changed.
Contact: this tribe knows your nation.
Contact: none yet. A land unit must introduce your nation first.
Trade: this unit may inspect the market here.
Trade: needs a land introduction to this tribe first.
Trade: only a loaded wagon or a loaded ship can trade.
Trade: the carrier must hold goods; passengers alone are not trade goods.
Trade: a ship can trade only from the sea beside a coastal settlement.
Trade: angry or hostile natives refuse trade.
Trade: uneasy natives refuse ship trade.
This carrier's expedition is open here.
No expedition is open here yet.
Sale slot unavailable: no more goods grow here.
The sale or gift changed or is no longer possible, so nothing was traded.
Give %d pieces of %s as a gift. No gold is paid.
Haggle: one request is still open in this expedition.
Haggle: the natives accepted, so the price includes the +10%%.
Haggle: the natives refused, so the original price stays.
Haggle: not available for these goods in this expedition.
No goods you carry can be sold or given here.
Open the market first; then you can sell or give goods.
The natives cannot pay for these goods now.
Second stage: after your sale or gift you may buy one of these goods.
Buy %s: %d in stock at %d gold each.
Discount: one request is still open for this purchase.
Discount: the natives accepted, so the price is 10%% lower.
Discount: the natives refused, so the original price stays.
No offered goods are in stock to buy here.
The purchase cannot be made now; you may still decline it.
You cannot pay for even one piece now.
You bought %d pieces of %s for %d gold.
The purchase changed or is no longer possible, so nothing was bought.
The purchase was declined. Nothing was bought.
The natives are %s. Chances: information %s%%, gold %s%%, death %s%%.
The natives are %s. This nation has met their chief before, so you learn the same information again. Nothing is drawn, and no gold or risk applies.
The chief gives you %d gold from the treasury of this settlement.
The natives kill your scout. It is lost.
The chief tells you about this settlement. Goods for sale: %s. Goods wanted: %s. Teachable skill: %s. The land within two squares is now marked on your map.
The chief repeats the same information. Goods for sale: %s. Goods wanted: %s. Teachable skill: %s. The land within two squares is marked on your map.
The chief visit changed, so nothing happened.
Owner: %s. Missionary: %s. The natives are %s. Progress: %d of %d updates. Each update lowers their alarm toward you by 2, or by 4 for an expert, and raises the alarm of each rival they know by 1.
The mission terms changed, so nothing happened.
Mission of %s: %s missionary. The natives are %s. Progress: %d of %d updates.

Rival mission of %s: its missionary is %s, and the natives are %s toward them. Your missionary is %s, and the natives are %s toward you. Your chance: %d%%. If you win, the rival missionary dies and yours takes the mission. If you lose, your missionary dies and the rival mission stays.
Your missionary won. The rival missionary died, and yours now holds the mission.
Your missionary lost and died. The rival mission stays.
The contest terms changed, so nothing happened.

Pay to turn the %s tribe against the European power you choose. On success the tribe pursues that power for a limited time, and stops sooner if its anger toward that power subsides. The price and your chance are shown before you confirm.
Price: %d gold, paid once whether the attempt succeeds or fails. Your missionary is %s, and the tribe is %s toward your nation. Your missions in this tribe: %d. Your chance: %d%%. Your gold: %d.
You do not have enough gold for this price, so the attempt cannot be confirmed.
This power cannot be chosen now.
Paid %d gold; you now have %d. The tribe has turned against %s and will pursue it for up to %d native turns, ending sooner if its anger fades.
Paid %d gold; you now have %d. The missionary failed to turn the tribe, so its earlier plans stand.
The incitement was refused because the terms changed or the price cannot be paid. Nothing was paid.
A %s learns %s after %d owner updates. Meanwhile the colonist stays with the natives and cannot move, work or fight.
A colonist learned %s from the natives.
The natives turned hostile, so the colonist left without learning %s.
A native convert joined your colony as an unassigned colonist.
A native convert returned to the tribe after eight turns without work.
Las Casas freed your existing native converts; they now work as ordinary colonists.
The offer or the situation changed, so nothing was started.
The colonist cannot leave yet: no free square beside the settlement.
The colonist could not leave now, so nothing changed.
Learned %s; the colonist waits to leave once a square beside the natives is free.
The natives turned hostile; the colonist waits to leave once a square beside them is free.
To choose the amount of goods, hold Ctrl while dragging on macOS, or Ctrl+Shift on Linux and Windows.
Native convert of the %s. Unassigned turns: %s of 8.
